instrument: COMPAS-W Wellbeing Scale — original 26-item adult measure
domains: Six dimensions: Composure; Own-worth; Mastery; Positivity; Achievement; Satisfaction. Composite mental wellbeing (hedonic + eudaimonic).
population: Australian healthy adult twins (n1669), 18–61 years; nonclinical origin, not a diagnosis.
research_evidence: Gatt JM et al., Psychiatry Research 2014 (online 2014-05-10, print 2014-09-30), DOI 10.1016/j.psychres.2014.04.033. Developed n=1669 Australian healthy adult twins age 18–61. Original scale 26 scored questions, 6 components; 12-month reliability total r=.82. May-2026 Frontiers corrigendum withdrew supplementary reproduction of proprietary 26 items; Jul-2026 SECOND correction corrected previous IP/commercial-licence wording; never rely on superseded May COI as current licence.
respondent_languages: No additional respondent-language validation claimed; published paper language or multi-country reuse does not establish approved translation rights.
commercial_digital_permission: RESEARCH_ONLY. Proprietary 26-item questionnaire: explicit author/rightsholder written approval required for copying items, commercial digital questionnaire hosting, scoring, translations and derivatives. May 27 2026 correction removed item reproduction; July 27 2026 correction superseded May conflict-of-interest ownership/licensing language. CC BY article terms do NOT grant stand-alone scale rights.
safety_notes: Original adult form only. 26 is not adolescent 23-item best-fit model; no item text reproduced, no clinical cutoffs or automated diagnosis; author-approved scoring, current IP verification, data governance and permission gate pending.

instrument: COMPAS-W Wellbeing Scale — empirically reduced 23-item Australian adolescent research model
items: 23 best-fit CFA (all 26 original items administered; 3 excluded)
domains: Six modeled wellbeing domains: Composure; Own-worth; Mastery; Positivity; Achievement; Satisfaction. Adolescent second-order total wellbeing; 23 retained items, some revised subscale associations.
population: Australian adolescents ages 13–17, N1078; mixed nonclinical and clinical/developmental cohorts; 23-item CFA is derived from 26 administered, not a new independent sample.
research_evidence: Lam JR, Park HRP, Gatt JM, Frontiers in Psychiatry 2024-06-27, DOI 10.3389/fpsyt.2024.1333828, N1078 adolescents ages 13–17, 79.13% nonclinical and 20.87% psychiatric/developmental clinical. Administered original 26, best fit reduced to 23; CFI .893/TLI .877, Own-worth alpha .601. May 2026 corrigendum removed published original scale wording; July 2026 correction superseded commercial licence ownership statement. Same cohort, NOT separate adolescent and adult data.
respondent_languages: Other adolescent countries' use does NOT prove respondent language validation; do not infer ZH, FR, PT from place names.
commercial_digital_permission: Proprietary family; commercial digital app use/derivatives require current rightsholder written authorization. CORRECTION HISTORY: 2026-05-27 removed leaked 26 items; 2026-07-27 rescinded prior conflict-of-interest claim of assignment and specific commercial licence pathway. Treat authorization/owner as unconfirmed pending direct rights review.
safety_notes: Research-only adolescent alternate factor model, NOT a ready-to-use 23-question questionnaire. Some fit/reliability limitations (CFI<.90; Own-worth alpha .601). No copied items/scoring/cutoffs, no minor-self-service deployment.

instrument: Mental Wellness Tool — original 13-item two-step transdiagnostic triage screen
items: 13 selected questions (3 initial broad screen plus 10 further classification candidates)
domains: First-step any mental disorder; second-step categories: common mental disorders, severe mental disorders, substance-use disorders, suicide risk. Triage classifications, NOT four psychometrically proven continuous latent subscales.
population: Adults in primary/general health facilities in Mozambique, N911 development + N453 validation, with psychiatric reference comparison.
research_evidence: Lovero KL et al., Psychiatric Services 2021-05-17 online, print 2021-08-01, DOI 10.1176/appi.ps.202000504. Mozambique six clinical facilities: development n911, validation n453. 13 chosen items from nine previous assessment instruments, requiring source-by-source copyright due diligence; original tool screening/triage validation, not stand-alone diagnostic verdict.
respondent_languages: Mozambique geography does not verify PT/PT-MZ questionnaire language or validated translation; no respondent translations counted.
commercial_digital_permission: RESEARCH_ONLY; clinically sensitive multidiagnostic and suicidality screen, items selected from nine third-party measures; seek author+source-rightsholder commercial digital hosting/translation and scoring permissions. Specialist clinical escalation and local practice validation mandatory; no self-service automated triage.
safety_notes: 2021 original length 13 vs some secondary reports of 3+9 or reduced-model sensitivity analyses; use full 13 as study main questionnaire; confirm final question wording, branching and prior item copyright. No patient-facing online activation.

instrument: Mental Wellness Tool — 2026 US psychiatric emergency-department validation of existing 13-item form
items: 13 (same questionnaire family as 2021; 3 initial broad-screen + 10 additional items)
domains: Any mental disorder screening in first 3 items; categorical triage for common mental disorder, severe mental disorder, substance use disorder and suicide risk. Not four independently validated dimensional subscale scores.
population: US psychiatric emergency department N269, sample-specific psychiatric triage comparison, not validated for nonclinical consumer self-assessment.
research_evidence: Sweetland AC et al., Psychiatric Services, first online 2026-09-03, print 2026-10-01, DOI 10.1176/appi.ps.20230560. US psychiatric ED adults N269. Initial 3-item screening any mental disorder sensitivity .95; whole 13-item classifications with varied specificity incl suicide risk .50; 2026 paper is a NEW POPULATION validation of same mwTool-13 family, not a separately invented scale.
respondent_languages: No other new independent respondent-language translations; US validation is a population extension, not a new translated edition.
commercial_digital_permission: RESEARCH_ONLY; copied questionnaire components may have separate owners, commercial web deployment not licensed. Psychiatric crisis and suicidal-risk false positives/negatives require clinician oversight, appropriate escalation and consent. Do not reuse study operating characteristics as general-population cutoffs.
safety_notes: Separate evidence entry SAME 13-item mwTool family, NOT second new questionnaire, not 13 new translated items; n269 single emergency setting, suicide-risk specificity .50. No clinical rollout or patient self-triage.
